advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Close the fd in `_acquire_fcntl` before `NoExclusiveLegError` propagates (e.g. wrap take_exclusive in try/except that closes fd, or catch (OSError, NoExclusiveLegError)).
evidence: lock.py:210 `_kernel.take_exclusive(fd)` then only `except OSError as exc:` at lock.py:212
lock_kernel.py:97 `class NoExclusiveLegError(RuntimeError):` — not an OSError, so the fd-closing `except OSError` at lock.py:218 is skipped on the no-leg path
Contrast: write_lock_is_busy (lock.py:258) and _probe_fcntl catch NoExclusiveLegError INSIDE a try/finally that runs `os.close(fd)`, so they do not leak — only the acquire path does
advisory.finding: In `_acquire_fcntl`, the fd from `os.open` is leaked when `take_exclusive` raises `NoExclusiveLegError`. That exception subclasses `RuntimeError` (not `OSError`), so the surrounding `except OSError` handler does not run and the fd is never closed before the exception propagates out of `acquire`.
scenarios: A platform with neither fcntl nor msvcrt importable (the exact case NoExclusiveLegError models): every acquire() call leaks one open fd before raising
advisory.suggested_fix: Wrap the `_kernel.take_exclusive(fd)` call so that a NoExclusiveLegError closes fd before propagating, e.g. add `except _kernel.NoExclusiveLegError: os.close(fd); raise` alongside the existing OSError handler.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a Windows-leg test asserting `_kernel.is_contention(OSError(errno.EDEADLK, ...))` is True (fcntl=None, msvcrt stubbed) so the EDEADLK contention membership is pinned.
evidence: In tests/unit/store/test_windows_exclusive_leg.py, `_windows_shaped_msvcrt().locking` raises `OSError(errno.EACCES, ...)` only — never EDEADLK — so `is_contention(OSError(errno.EDEADLK))` under the Windows leg (fcntl=None) is never asserted.

The retargeted errno tests in tests/unit/test_lock_stale_reclaim.py patch `_kernel.fcntl.flock` while `_kernel.fcntl is not None`, so they exercise only the POSIX branch of `is_contention` (`_POSIX_CONTENTION`), not the Windows branch.
advisory.finding: The Windows-leg contention set adds `errno.EDEADLK` as a distinct contention errno, but no test exercises `is_contention` returning True for an EDEADLK OSError under the Windows leg. The `windows_leg` fixture's stubbed `msvcrt.locking` raises only `EACCES` (which is contention on BOTH platforms), so the Windows-specific EDEADLK membership is never driven; a regression that dropped `errno.EDEADLK` from `_WINDOWS_CONTENTION` would turn a merely-contended lock into an immediately re-raised OSError on Windows and no test would fail.
advisory.suggested_fix: Under the windows_leg fixture (fcntl=None, msvcrt stubbed), assert `_kernel.is_contention(OSError(errno.EDEADLK, 'deadlock'))` is True and, as a negative control, `_kernel.is_contention(OSError(errno.ENOLCK, 'x'))` is False.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting `_kernel.leg_name()` returns 'fcntl.flock' / 'msvcrt.locking' / 'none' for the three fcntl/msvcrt handle configurations.
